description: Remember something for later in a business's Foundry ontology: what an agent learned, decided or did, sent as JSON pieces (objects with an id) to a Foundry API source (a connector of kind events), which the ontologies reading the source take into their graph, to read and ask about later. A piece replaces any piece already in the source with the same id. Not confirmed: it only writes data to a source a person made. Anyone who can send to the source can replace any of its pieces by id, or blank its fields by sending {}. Apps without an MCP client can POST the same pieces to https://ingest.helix-db.com/v1/sources/<event_source_id>/pieces with a send token as the bearer.

client_token.description: A new random value for each call, 16 to 64 printable ASCII characters (a UUID). Reuse it only to retry the same call with the same pieces, such as after backend_unavailable: that stores nothing new and returns the first send. With other pieces it is refused.

event_source_id.description: The API source: a connector of kind events. With a send token, optional: the token's own.

pieces.description: 1 to 500 pieces, at most 1 MiB of data together (keep a call under about 800 KB: data_json is escaped inside the call).

data_json.description: The piece: one JSON object as text, at most 256 KiB, nested at most 64 deep. Its top-level keys are the source's fields; a field keeps the JSON type it first had (null is always allowed). It may not have top-level id, received_at or occurred_at. Write it from the original text; integers above 2^53 go as strings if your client may have parsed them.

id.description: 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters, no spaces, unique in the source: a later piece with the same id replaces it, whoever sent it.

use_case_run_id.description: An open run of a use case (helix_foundry_start_use_case_run) to record this send under, with its pieces' ids; empty for none.

workspace_id.description: The API source's workspace. With a send token, optional: the token's own.

name: helix_foundry_send_pieces

capacity.description: rows, max_rows, bytes and max_bytes (strings of digits) and percent_full of the source's table.

next.description: Pieces reach the source's table at its next sync, about a minute away; ontologies that map it see them at their next refresh.

replayed.description: True when this client_token's send was already stored: nothing new was stored.

seq.description: The send's number in the source, as a string of digits.

warning.description: Set from 80% full; tell the user.

title: Send pieces to an API source
